title: How a load of salt was weighed (fixture)
text: Salt was weighed dry: wet salt carries water, so an honest weight starts with drying a ground sample on an iron plate and weighing it again. A tally kept on the wet weight overstates the salt. Scales were tested against a brass standard, and a trader who doubted a tally could ask for a public weighing.

claims.text: Wet salt carries water, so it must be dried before an honest weighing.
claims.evidence: for wet salt may carry a tenth part of its weight in water

claims.text: The sample is ground and weighed before and after warming.
claims.evidence: grinds it, and weighs it before and after it is warmed on an iron plate

claims.text: A tally on the wet weight overstates the salt.
claims.evidence: A tally that records the wet weight will always overstate the salt.

claims.text: A trader could demand a public weighing.
claims.evidence: A trader could demand a public weighing before the masters if she believed a tally false.
